name: Foundry Local
what: Microsoft's local inference runtime: an ONNX Runtime daemon with an OpenAI-compatible service, a catalog of ONNX models tuned per device (CPU, CUDA, WebGPU, Intel and Qualcomm NPUs), and the `foundry` command line that starts the server, downloads models and loads or unloads them. Preview software; the daemon picks a port unless told one.
licence: Microsoft Software License Terms for the runtime; MIT for the SDK repository

detect.note: the daemon assigns a port each start unless started with --port; a unit needs the fixed one (foundry server start --port <port> --idle-timeout 0). Models come from Microsoft's catalog by alias; a unit's model_id is the alias or the model id as `foundry model list` shows it.

endpoints.cli: foundry server start|stop|status, foundry model load|unload|list --loaded

can: start the daemon on the unit's fixed port and stop it
load a model by alias and unload it, through the command line
see what is loaded (foundry model list --loaded)
cannot: see busy: neither the CLI nor /openai/status says so
serve a model that is not in Microsoft's catalog, or a GGUF
run on Linux: Windows and Apple Silicon only (2026-10 docs)
drive.note: Table from the CLI reference of 2026-10 (learn.microsoft.com, foundry-local/reference/reference-cli). The loaded_re is a guess at the list's layout and is the first thing to check when someone drives it. Not yet driven from any machine.

never: --idle-timeout left at its default for a unit: the daemon stops itself after a quiet spell and the unit reads as down

update.note: winget upgrade --id Microsoft.FoundryLocal on Windows; brew upgrade microsoft/foundrylocal/foundrylocal on macOS. The execution-provider plugins update themselves.

windows: foundry model list (first run downloads the execution providers for your hardware)
macos: brew tap microsoft/foundrylocal && brew install foundrylocal

good: small models on an NPU or a laptop GPU with no setup beyond winget
a Windows machine that wants an OpenAI endpoint from Microsoft's own catalog, with the vendor's execution providers
not: anything outside the catalog, or a model file you already have
a sovereign setup: the catalog, the execution providers and their updates come from Microsoft's servers on first use
large models: the catalog is small and quantized for devices
